messages:
sara-support: FYI customer ACME hitting lots of 504s and long tail timeouts for hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. They say it started after a marketing campaign.

acme-sre: Repro steps: send repeated chat completions with long context (~6k tokens) at ~120 rps. After ~2 minutes we see 504s and 30s timeouts. Here's a minimal curl we used:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-8k","input":"<6k tokens>"}'
```

acme-sre: Also attaching a sampling of gateway logs (trimmed):
```
[09:12:23] request_id=aa12 enqueue_delay_ms=2100 queue_depth=1024 batch_backlog=37
[09:12:24] request_id=aa13 enqueue_delay_ms=3200 queue_depth=1024 early_reject=true status=504
[09:12:25] request_id=aa20 dequeue_duration_ms=4800 kvcache_miss=true
```

mike-oncall: Thanks. queue_depth=1024 stands out — that's exactly the configured per-host soft limit. Looks like continuous-batcher backlog + large seq lengths blew past effective throughput.

jen-support: Customer reporting 504s at ~30s, consistent with gateway deadline. They want ETA/mitigation asap.

mike-oncall: Short-term mitigations we can try: 1) reduce continuous_batching.window_ms to lower batching latency, 2) temporarily bump dedicated workers for hosted region (if capacity), 3) enable early-fallback to smaller model variant for requests that hit kv/cache misses.

eva-runtime: I pulled runtime metrics — batch_backlog_count spiked to 42 on the affected pool, and avg_batch_size jumped from 8->20 because large sequences prevent effective packing. Also observed high kvcache_eviction_rate.

raj-ml: Large sequences mean more KV cache misses on hot requests; continuous batching groups them so some requests wait longer. We should avoid overpacking long-seq requests with small ones. Suggest a quick classifier to mark long-seq as "longseq" and route to a separate fast-path with smaller batching.

mike-oncall: For immediate action I'm going to: 1) lower window_ms from 50->20 on the hosted pool, 2) enable small-model fallback policy for the route, 3) temporarily raise queue_depth soft limit to 1536 if infra has headroom. Starting now. @deploy-bot can you run the change?

deploy-bot: Triggering config change: continuous-batcher.window_ms=20 for pool-hosted-us-east-1 (canary). Rolling to 10% of hosts.

deploy-bot: Canary successful on 10% (20 hosts). No errors observed. Monitoring p95 for the canary hosts.

acme-sre: After canary we see p95 drop from 18s->7s for canary hosts. Non-canary still suffering.

mike-oncall: Rolling to 60% now.

deploy-bot: Rolled to 60%. Metric delta: overall queue_depth down 40% on changed hosts, batch_backlog down.

eva-runtime: Observed fewer kvcache evictions and lower enqueue_delay_ms on canary hosts. Good signal.

mike-oncall: Also increased soft queue_depth to 1536 for the pool. That reduced early_reject=true events but we need longer-term fix for long sequences.

jen-support: Customer confirms 504 rate dropped to near zero and they're seeing acceptable latency. They asked what happened and what we'll change permanently.

raj-ml: Long-term: 1) route long-seq requests to dedicated fast-path (smaller batches, higher mem), 2) implement request-size-aware batching window and kvcache-prioritization, 3) add per-tenant burst allowance so marketing spikes don't fully starve other tenants.

mike-oncall: Opened incident ticket INC-2026 and assigned to eng-runtime + product to scope routing/fast-path work. Also adding immediate playbook updates: - runbook step to flip window_ms and queue_depth, - when backlog>30 escalate to runtime team.

sara-support: Noting timeline and customer comms — will send summary to ACME and mark as resolved once postmortem scheduled.

acme-sre: Thanks for the quick turnaround. Please keep me posted on permanent changes.

mike-oncall: Postmortem owner: @eva-runtime. ETA for design doc: EOW. Follow-up actions: CH1: implement request classifier (raj-ml), CH2: routing policy (eng-runtime), CH3: console alert for batch_backlog>20 (devex).

jen-support: I'll send the customer status note now. :thumbsup:

sara-support: Closing thread updates here; will append link to postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
